title: Practical Psychomancy and Crystal Gazing: A Course of Lessons on the Psychic Phenomena of Distant Sensing, Clairvoyance, Psychometry, Crystal Gazing, etc.
author: William Walker Atkinson
edition_cited: Project Gutenberg eBook #43954 (released 2013), from the Chicago: Advanced Thought Publishing Co. edition
locator_hints: Lesson on how to develop oneself: list of early signs incl. 'colored clouds floating before their eyes in the dark, before they sink to rest' (c. 13% into file)
Lesson on crystal gazing: visualise a familiar object, then try to reproduce it in the crystal; first signs 'cloudiness' or 'milky-mist' (c. 20%)
Lesson quoting a writer on scrying with a glass of water: look two or three minutes without tiring, 'winking as much as you please' (c. 43%)
summary: A popular course that compiles the period's advice. For crystal gazing Atkinson recommends first practising mental picturing of a familiar object and then trying to reproduce the picture in the crystal, claiming this 'will often gradually lead to actual seeing'. He gives the first sign of actual seeing as a cloudiness or milky mist in the crystal that slowly resolves into a form 'like the precipitation of a photograph' in a developing room. A quoted authority advises a plain glass of water in subdued light, looked at for two or three minutes without strain and with free blinking, thought fixed on what one wishes to see; 'if you have the faculty' the glass clouds with a milky mist. Among spontaneous early signs of psychic development he lists faces, landscapes or coloured clouds floating before the eyes in the dark before sleep.
why_relevant: States an explicit bridge from deliberate visualisation to seen imagery in the crystal, and repeats the milky-mist onset sign; useful as evidence of how the instruction circulated.

date_evidence.basis: Project Gutenberg #43954 header and transcribed title page; warm-up WebSearch result listed the same Gutenberg text; print year 1908 as catalogued, not re-verified from a scan

notes: Largely derivative: long unattributed or loosely attributed quotations (Leadbeater on the aura, Stead/Lang on scrying). Low priority unless the visualisation-to-seeing claim is wanted.
